tip: Melhor is the irregular comparative of bom, so 'better' is melhor, never mais bom: será um dia melhor.
Vamos plus an infinitive is the everyday future in Brazil, easier than the simple future: nós vamos reformar.
Quem chegar uses the future subjunctive; for regular verbs it looks just like the infinitive, chegar.
In reported speech, the conditional viria expresses a future seen from the past: ele disse que viria.
The conditional ending -ia is the same for -ar, -er and -ir verbs, so escolher becomes escolheria.
Tentar is followed directly by the infinitive, with no preposition: vou tentar resolver isso.
A gente means 'we' but takes a singular verb, so it is a gente vai, never a gente vamos.
Importar-se de means 'to mind'; keep both the reflexive se and de: vocês se importariam de esperar.
Tudo o que means 'everything that'; the little o links tudo to the relative que: tudo o que eu quero.
Cortar o cabelo means 'get a haircut', even when the barber does it; Portuguese keeps the active verb.
Buscar means 'pick someone up', not just 'search': vou te buscar no aeroporto.
Ter coragem de plus an infinitive means 'to dare to': teria coragem de pular.
Parar de plus an infinitive means 'to stop doing something': parar de fumar.
O ano que vem is the everyday way to say 'next year', literally 'the year that comes'.
Cujo means 'whose' and agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: a casa cujo telhado vazou.
When o attaches to an infinitive ending in r, the r drops and a circumflex is added: receber plus o becomes recebê-lo.
Será que opens a question meaning 'I wonder' or 'do you think': será que vai chover hoje?
For hypotheticals, pair the conditional with se plus the imperfect subjunctive: eu moraria no Rio se pudesse.
Promoção means a store sale or special offer, not a job promotion: a loja vai fazer uma promoção.
Use ficar, not ser, for becoming happy or sad: eu ficaria muito feliz.
The verb assistir takes a when it means 'to watch', so it is assistir ao filme, not assistir o filme.
Programa is masculine even though it ends in -a: o programa que assistimos.
The crase joins a plus a into à before a feminine noun: nós iríamos à praia.
